documentMetadata.title: Health Data Metric Standards (HDMS) - Reference Frame for Capturing, Analyzing, and Publishing Health Data
documentMetadata.normativeLanguageStandard: RFC 2119 (MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, MAY)
usageNotes: MUST: every conforming implementation shall satisfy; SHOULD: deviations require documented justification; MAY: optional.

Terminology codes in this document are reference bindings curated from published releases. Before production use, every binding MUST be re-validated against the current LOINC, SNOMED CT, ICD, and RxNorm releases via a terminology server (rule G-TERM-01).
Extend the catalog only through the governance workflow in section framework.governance; never fork the standard silently.
designPrinciples: Patient safety first: every metric must carry clinically valid interpretation and safety-critical limits.
Standards-native: bind to FHIR, LOINC, SNOMED CT, UCUM rather than inventing local semantics.
Single source of truth: the metric registry is authoritative; all pipelines consume registry-approved definitions only.
Privacy by design: privacy tier assigned at metric definition time, not at publication time.
Algorithmic fairness: AI/ML models and derived metrics must be evaluated for bias and disparate impact before deployment.
Future-proof interoperability: align with FHIR R5, OMOP CDM v6, and emerging global health data spaces.
Quantitative management: every process in the data lifecycle has measurable performance objectives and control charts.
Continuous optimization: defects trigger causal analysis; improvements are institutionalized, not local patches.
Equity: metrics must be capable of stratification to detect and eliminate disparities.

keywords.SHOULD: strong recommendation; deviation requires ADR (architecture decision record)

inScope: person-level clinical measurements, laboratory results, vital signs, patient-reported outcomes
social determinants of health (SDOH) and environmental exposure metrics
derived clinical, epidemiological, and AI/ML model performance indicators
healthcare delivery quality and operational metrics
population health and public health surveillance metrics
metadata, governance, quality, privacy, and process-control standards for the above
outOfScope: imaging pixel-level interpretation (managed via DICOM standards separately)

metricLifecycleStates.definition: engineering and quality review of value domain, validation, FHIR binding
CTB verification of definition, ranges, evidence; terminology server validation executed
superseded; consumers MUST migrate within notice window
no longer serviced; historical data retained per retention schedule

approvalChecklist: terminology binding validated against current release (G-TERM-01)

validation rules selected from the validation rule library

AI/ML metrics: fairness baseline and drift monitoring plan defined (if applicable)

requirements: all registered consumers notified via registry changelog

governance.disputeResolution: unresolved issues escalate to DGC with written position papers from MRB and CTB; decision minuted in registry

rules: every state transition MUST be recorded in an immutable audit trail (who, what, when, source system, outcome)
data in 'captured' state MUST NOT be used for primary clinical or published analytics until 'validated'
records flagged entered-in-error MUST be retained and flagged, never hard-deleted (FHIR-compatible)
synthetic data generated for testing MUST pass fidelity and privacy guarantee checks before leaving the secure environment

retention.clinicalRecordData: per jurisdiction (typical 7-10 years; pediatrics until age of majority plus limitation period)

compatibilityRules: consumers MUST be able to pin any exact version of any metric
MAJOR metric version bumps require simultaneous registry migration note
the standard version and metric versions evolve independently

dataTypes.serialization: JSON number or string; no exponent notation; trailing zeros preserved end-to-end
{value: decimal, unit: UCUM-code}; unit is mandatory
{low: quantity|null, high: quantity|null, lowInclusive: boolean, highInclusive: boolean}
{system: uri, code: string, display: string}; system MUST be one of foundations.terminology.systemUris
UTF-8 free text; never enters aggregate publication without review
RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 with UTC offset; stored canonically in UTC
decimal 0..1 or percent 0..100 with declared unit '%'
integer on a declared instrument scale with documented anchor points
JSON array of homogeneous types (e.g., array of coded)

missingDataPolicy.principle: absence MUST be explicit; sentinel values (0, -1, 999, empty string) are FORBIDDEN to encode missingness
missingDataPolicy.reporting: missingness rate per metric MUST be reported in every published dataset dictionary

units.mandate: all quantitative values MUST carry a UCUM 2.1 code; free-text units are FORBIDDEN
units.canonicalStorage: store native measured unit; analytics converts to the metric's canonical unit using appendix.conversionFactors; conversion MUST be logged with factor version

bindingRules: G-TERM-01: every coded field MUST bind to the preferred system for its domain and MUST be validated via a terminology server at build time and at runtime ingestion
G-TERM-02: local codes MUST ship with a FHIR ConceptMap to a standard system; unmapped local codes are a DQ-03 defect
G-TERM-03: value sets MUST be versioned, OID-assigned, and exportable in VSAC-compatible format
G-TERM-04: SNOMED CT edition (International or national extension) MUST be declared per deployment

metricSchema.description: every metric object in catalog.metrics conforms to this field contract

fields.name: terminology
fields.required: for coded/observable metrics; LOINC key mandatory for lab and vital observables

fields.name: interpretation
fields.required: clinical classes or reference ranges with evidence source

captureProtocols.name: Office/Ambulatory Blood Pressure
steps: patient seated 5 minutes, back supported, legs uncrossed
arm supported at heart level, correct cuff size
no caffeine, exercise, or smoking for 30 minutes prior
obtain 2 readings at least 1 minute apart; record both and the average
constraints: use device validated per ISO 81060-2 or equivalent
record cuff size, arm, and posture as provenance

captureProtocols.name: Heart Rate
steps: radial or apical pulse counted 30-60 seconds
state rhythm regularity as provenance
for wearables, require photoplethysmography validation evidence

captureProtocols.name: Respiratory Rate
steps: count full 60 seconds without announcing the count
record patient state (rest, sleeping, distressed)
constraints: automated capnography accepted with device metadata

captureProtocols.name: Body Temperature
steps: record route (oral, tympanic, temporal, axillary, rectal, core)
apply route-specific normal interpretation
constraints: routes MUST NOT be mixed in trend analysis without route normalization

captureProtocols.name: Pulse Oximetry
steps: warm, perfused digit; motion minimized
average over >= 30 seconds
record device model and firmware
constraints: note pigment-related accuracy bias in interpretation (equity requirement)

captureProtocols.name: Height, Weight, BMI
steps: stadiometer head in Frankfort plane
calibrated scale, light clothing, no shoes
BMI computed as weight_kg / height_m^2 at metric precision

captureProtocols.name: Waist Circumference (WHO protocol)
steps: midpoint between lower rib margin and iliac crest
tape snug, horizontal, at end of normal expiration
two readings within 1 cm; record mean

captureProtocols.name: Venipuncture and Specimen Handling
steps: correct tube type and order of draw per CLSI GP41
label at bedside with two identifiers
process within stability window per analyte
constraints: fasting metrics require >= 8 h fast, water permitted, recorded as provenance

captureProtocols.name: Spirometry (ATS/ERS 2019)
steps: 3 acceptable maneuvers; best 2 within 150 mL repeatability
report pre- and post-bronchodilator separately
apply GLI reference equations

captureProtocols.name: 12-Lead ECG
steps: 10-second recording, 25 mm/s, 10 mm/mV
electrode placement per AHA/ACCF/HRS recommendations
constraints: interval measurements must state algorithm manufacturer

captureProtocols.name: Patient-Reported Outcome Administration
steps: instruments administered electronically where possible with identical item wording and order
recall window stated in question text
language versions must be certified translations
constraints: PROs are never imputed from other data for clinical use

captureProtocols.name: Pediatric Measurement
steps: recumbent length < 24 months; standing height >= 24 months
head circumference per WHO technique
growth interpretation uses WHO Child Growth Standards (0-5 y) and WHO Reference 5-19 y
constraints: growth percentiles, not raw values, drive clinical interpretation

captureProtocols.name: SDOH Screening Administration
steps: administer validated tool (e.g., Gravity Project, CMS HRSN) in private setting
use certified translation if language preference is not primary
document patient consent for community referral
constraints: responses MUST NOT be used for care denial or punitive administrative actions
linkage to community resources requires explicit patient consent

validationRuleLibrary.rule: value within metric permittedRange; violations flagged, not auto-corrected
unit code resolvable in UCUM and equal to a metric-allowed unit
duplicate detection on (patient, metric, effectiveDateTime, value); duplicates quarantined
effectiveDateTime not in future and within capture-protocol timing constraints
within-subject change exceeds physiologic delta threshold -> specialist review queue
cross-field: systolic MUST be strictly greater than diastolic for the same measurement event
cross-field: BMI consistent with height/weight within rounding tolerance
device calibration current at capture time; expired calibration quarantines data for regulated use
local laboratory reference range binding current; expired ranges block result interpretation
missing values use only allowed DataAbsentReason codes
patient identity resolved to golden record before validation completes
source, actor, device, and timestamp present; else record fails DQ-10

metrics.name: Systolic Blood Pressure
metrics.definition: Peak arterial pressure during left ventricular systole, measured non-invasively at the brachial artery.
evidence: Whelton PK et al., Hypertension. 2018;71:e13-e115 (2017 ACC/AHA Guideline)

metrics.name: Housing Stability
metrics.definition: Assessment of patient's current housing situation and risk of homelessness, per Gravity Project standards.

notes: Positive screens trigger referral workflows to community-based organizations

metrics.name: Model Fairness Disparity Ratio
metrics.definition: Ratio of a model's performance metric (e.g., F1-score, True Positive Rate) for a protected demographic group compared to the reference group.

interpretation.source: NIST AI RMF, WHO Ethics Guidelines

evidence: WHO Ethics and Governance of AI for Health

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.definition: proportion of expected required values that are present and non-missing

dimensions.name: Accuracy
dimensions.definition: concordance with an accepted reference (re-abstraction sample, gold-standard instrument)

dimensions.name: Conformance (Validity)
dimensions.definition: proportion of values conforming to type, unit, format, and terminology binding

dimensions.name: Consistency
dimensions.definition: proportion of records passing cross-field and cross-source rules (e.g., VR-X-SBP-DBP)

dimensions.name: Timeliness
dimensions.definition: latency from clinical event to availability in the validated store

dimensions.name: Uniqueness
dimensions.definition: absence of duplicate records for the same real-world fact

dimensions.name: Referential Integrity
dimensions.definition: proportion of foreign-key references resolvable (patient, encounter, device, terminology codes)

dimensions.name: Precision Concordance
dimensions.definition: values reported to the metric-declared decimal places with unit conformance at 100 percent

dimensions.name: Plausibility
dimensions.definition: proportion of values within physiologic or logically expected bounds; outliers flagged for review

dimensions.name: Provenance Completeness
dimensions.definition: records carrying complete source, actor, device, and timestamp provenance

dimensions.name: Fairness
dimensions.definition: absence of unjustified disparate impact across protected demographic groups in derived metrics or AI models

dimensions.name: Explainability
dimensions.definition: proportion of AI-driven metric outputs accompanied by interpretable feature attributions or confidence intervals

qualityGates.rule: batch or stream MUST pass DQ-03, DQ-07, DQ-10 >= threshold before entering validated store
dataset MUST publish a DQ scorecard covering all 12 dimensions before it may feed analyses or publications
published outputs MUST pass small-cell suppression and de-identification verification (see publicationStandards)
AI/ML models MUST pass DQ-11 (Fairness) and DQ-12 (Explainability) thresholds and AIB sign-off before production promotion

severity.definition: patient-safety-relevant, published-output corruption, or severe algorithmic bias
materially wrong values reaching analysis or model performance degradation

defectManagement.verification: every corrective action MUST be verified by re-measuring the owning DQ dimension over >= 30 days or >= 1 full cycle before closure

requirements: structured capture preferred over free text
default unit and range enforced in UI
device identifier, serial, calibration state recorded
clock synchronization within 1 second via NTP
raw sensor retention configurable with privacy tier respected
activity-state context mandatory for heart-rate metrics
cross-walk table to clinical codes maintained and versioned

temporalStandards.canonicalTime: UTC storage; RFC 3339 with offset at the edge
temporalStandards.clockSync: NTP across capture devices; drift > 2 seconds blocks regulated capture (VR-CAL extension)
temporalStandards.eventTimeVsProcessingTime: both recorded; analytics uses event time by default
temporalStandards.effectiveVsIssued: FHIR Observation.effectiveDateTime is the clinical time; authored/issued times retained as provenance

personIdentity.goldenRecord: master patient index with deterministic and probabilistic matching
rules: overlays (false positives) tracked as SEV2 identity defects

enteredInError.policy: never delete; flag per FHIR entered-in-error; exclude from all analytics via semantic filter, not manual deletion

descriptive: report n for every group; never present percentages without denominators
use median and IQR for skewed distributions; mean and SD only when approximately normal or n large with caveat
state distributional assumptions and how they were checked

aggregationRules.rule: aggregation MUST respect metric permittedRange semantics: rates aggregate by weighted denominators, never by averaging rates
ISO 8601 week/month boundaries; timezone declared for day boundaries
derived metric version recorded with every aggregate (formula version + input dataset hash)

smallCellSuppression.complementarySuppression: apply to prevent back-calculation of suppressed cells
alternatives: differential privacy for public tables with governed epsilon

approvedModels: CMS hierarchical logistic models for readmissions
requirements: assessed for performance across demographic subgroups (bias testing)

standardization.direct: requires stable age-specific rates; declare standard population (WHO 2000-2025 or US 2000)
standardization.indirect: SMR = observed / expected; use when sparse counts
standardization.presentation: always accompany standardized values with crude rates and confidence intervals

missingDataAnalysis.imputation: multiple imputation with m >= 5 using chained equations for MAR; no single mean imputation for primary analyses; PROs and SDOH never imputed for clinical decisions
missingDataAnalysis.reporting: report complete-case and imputed results; Rubin pooling rules for MI

outlierPolicy.policy: flag-and-review; silent deletion FORBIDDEN; every exclusion logged with rule id and reviewer

statisticalProcessControl.purpose: CMMI Level 4/5 quantitative management of data processes and clinical metric performance
statisticalProcessControl.capability: Cp/Cpk computed for stable capture subprocesses; minimum requirement Cpk >= 1.33 for safety-critical capture
statisticalProcessControl.stabilityRules: Nelson rules 1-8 evaluated on every control chart; any rule violation opens a CAR ticket

rules.description: one point beyond 3 sigma from centerline
nine points on same side of centerline
six points steadily increasing or decreasing
fourteen points alternating up and down
two of three consecutive points beyond 2 sigma, same side
four of five consecutive points beyond 1 sigma, same side
fifteen points within 1 sigma, both sides (stratification)
eight points beyond 1 sigma, both sides (mixture)

inferential.effectSizes: report effect size with every test (RR, OR, HR, mean difference, SMD) plus 95% CI; p-values alone are insufficient
multiplicity: Bonferroni or hierarchical testing for confirmatory claims
inferential.survival: Kaplan-Meier with log-rank; Cox PH with Schoenfeld residual proportionality check
inferential.clusteredData: mixed-effects models with appropriate random effects (e.g., hospital); report ICC
inferential.causalLanguage: causal claims require design justification (target trial emulation, DAGs); associational language otherwise

modelGovernance.registry: all predictive models registered with training data hash, feature list, metrics, owner, and review date
monitoring: data drift via Population Stability Index (PSI) per feature
subgroup fairness metrics (demographic parity, equalized odds) quarterly
modelGovernance.retraining: triggered by drift thresholds or scheduled review; retrained models require AIB approval before promotion
modelGovernance.humanOversight: clinical decision support outputs MUST keep clinician-in-the-loop and display base rates and uncertainty
modelGovernance.frameworkAlignment: NIST AI RMF (Map, Measure, Manage, Govern) and EU AI Act high-risk system requirements

requirements: deterministic seeds for all stochastic steps
dataset and code versioning (dataset hash + repo commit)
analyses feeding publications preregistered where feasible
peer review of analysis code for regulatory-grade outputs

fairPrinciples.F: F1 persistent unique identifiers (DOI for datasets, UUID for entities); F2 rich metadata; F3 metadata includes the data identifier; F4 indexed in searchable registry
fairPrinciples.A: A1 retrievable by standard protocol (HTTPS/FHIR); A1.1 open for public tier, authenticated for restricted tiers; A2 metadata retained even when data deaccessioned
fairPrinciples.I: I1 standard vocabularies (LOINC/SNOMED/UCUM URIs); I2 FHIR resource references; I3 qualified cross-references to other datasets
fairPrinciples.R: R1 provenance (W3C PROV), license, and community standards (this standard) declared; R1.1 lineage of every derived field; R1.2 access-use conditions; R1.3 community-endorsed guidelines cited

controls: limited dataset per HIPAA limited data set

formats.use: bulk export ($export); one line per resource; UTF-8
tabular exchange; UTF-8; comma-delimited; RFC 3339 timestamps; dot decimal separator
API and registry outputs; Problem Details (RFC 9457) for errors

rules: legal/ethical holds freeze publication of affected cohorts
quality scores below G2 gate block publication until remediated

specifications: FHIR Bulk Data Access for population export
security: OAuth 2.0 scopes aligned to US Core (patient/*.read, user/*.read)

regulatoryBasis.applies: EU personal data including health data
high-risk AI systems in healthcare, transparency, and human oversight
voluntary framework for trustworthy AI development and deployment

safeHarbor18: 2 geographic subdivisions smaller than state (first 3 ZIP digits allowed only if region population > 20,000)
3 all date elements except year, including birth, admission, discharge, death; ages > 89 aggregated to 90+
12 vehicle identifiers and serial numbers including plates
16 biometric identifiers including finger and voice prints
18 any other unique identifying number, characteristic, or code
deidentification.expertDetermination: alternative pathway with documented statistically-grounded very small risk assessment

formalModels.governance: epsilon budget owned by PSB; consumption logged per release
requires utility score >= 0.85 and privacy leakage risk < 0.01 per PSB-approved evaluation

privacyTiers.name: Highly sensitive
controls: explicit consent scope (42 CFR Part 2, HIV, genetics, reproductive, behavioral health, SDOH)

technicalControls.encryptionAtRest: AES-256 (GCM preferred); keys in HSM/KMS with rotation <= 12 months
technicalControls.encryptionInTransit: TLS 1.2 minimum, TLS 1.3 preferred; mutual TLS for system-to-system regulated flows
technicalControls.accessControl: RBAC plus attribute-based conditions; MFA mandatory; session timeout 15 minutes for PT-2/PT-3
technicalControls.secretsAndKeys: no secrets in code; automated rotation; quarterly access recertification
technicalControls.vulnerabilityManagement: annual penetration test; continuous scanning; critical findings remediated <= 30 days

audit.review: automated anomaly alerts (off-hours bulk access, VIP records, unusual export volume, model retraining without approval)

notification: GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable
HIPAA breach notification per 60-day rule with 4-factor risk assessment
incidentResponse.exercises: semiannual tabletop including a data-integrity (not only confidentiality) and AI-model-poisoning scenario

coveredBy: PSB approval workflow for new high-risk processing

NIST SP 800-53 Rev.5 families AC, AU, IA, SC, SI, CM

all SEV1/SEV2 defects and control-chart signals require root-cause analysis and verified corrective action
annual portfolio of data-quality and cycle-time improvements selected from performance baselines and benchmarking
this standard is the governed data asset; registry, lineage, and retention managed per DM practices

quantitativeObjectives.definition: confirmed defects per 1,000 records in validated store
defects found downstream of G2 gate
share of active metrics with live control charts
rework + remediation + opportunity cost, currency units per quarter
percentage of deployed models meeting DQ-11 threshold

defectPrevention: poka-yoke at capture: UI-enforced units, ranges, and required context fields
terminology server validation at authoring time prevents invalid bindings (G-TERM-01)
schema contracts and CI data-contract tests block breaking changes
simulation and synthetic datasets validate pipelines before production data
checklists embedded in deployment runbooks derived from Pareto of historical defect classes
